scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of three robed men on a path through golden grain. The central man rubs a grain head over his cupped palm, the man on the left eats kernels, and the man behind holds a stalk. Low hills and a distant village lie beneath a blue sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined Galilean setting focuses on the disciples’ hand-plucking, rubbing and eating described in the verse. The three visible men represent disciples; Jesus remains outside the frame. Their appearance and the landscape are artistic choices. The Sabbath is supplied by the verse and is not separately pictured.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of robed adults and children standing beside a sunlit village lane, with stone and plaster houses, wooden doors, clay jars, an olive tree, and a blue lake beneath distant hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The open lane into the village and reflective listeners imaginatively connect the completed teaching with Jesus entering Capernaum. Jesus remains outside the frame. The people, buildings, and arrangement are illustrative details, not descriptions supplied by the verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A watercolor crowd of smiling, attentive men, women and children sits closely together on a rocky lakeshore beneath an olive tree, looking toward someone outside the frame. Blue water, reeds, distant hills and small stone buildings fill the background.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative lakeshore gathering emphasizes the crowd's eagerness to hear God's word while keeping Jesus outside the picture. The close grouping evokes their pressing near; the seated poses, clothing, tree and landscape details are artistic choices, not details specified by the verse. The image does not depict the later fishing miracle. Human artwork review remains pending.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of twelve male companions and three villagers listening toward the upper left beside sunlit stone houses. Sandals, walking staffs and travel bags suggest a journey; an olive-shaded road winds toward a distant hill settlement. A woman and child sit beside clay jars.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined village pause connects the attentive companions and residents with Jesus proclaiming the kingdom of God. Jesus remains outside the frame to the left. The winding road and distant settlement suggest His travels through cities and villages; the specific listeners, buildings and moment are artistic choices, not details supplied by the verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three pairs of men in simple tunics and earth-colored mantles walk along branching stone-lined paths toward hillside villages. The nearest pair turns toward one another as they walk. Olive trees, wildflowers and pale stone houses fill the warm watercolor landscape.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The three visible pairs represent some of the seventy whom the Lord sent ahead two by two. Their paths toward separate settlements picture the destinations of that sending. The landscape, clothing and gestures are imaginative setting details; Jesus is outside the frame, and the image does not attempt to show all seventy.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three bearded men in long cream tunics and earth-colored mantles stand beneath an olive tree. The foremost man rests one hand on his chest and extends an open palm toward the right, while the other two watch attentively. Warm sunlight falls across limestone rocks, wildflowers, distant hills and a small village.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The foremost disciple imaginatively represents the request to learn prayer after Jesus finished praying. All three look toward Jesus outside the frame; no visible figure stands for Him. The olive tree, landscape, village and number of companions are artistic choices because the verse names neither the place nor the group size. John is mentioned in the request but is not depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three robed listeners look toward the left amid a tightly packed crowd in a sunlit stone courtyard. A clay bowl of bubbly dough, a small piece of starter and a striped linen cloth rest on a floured wooden board in the foreground, beneath grapevines and olive branches.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The crowded courtyard recalls the multitude pressing together, while the foreground listeners suggest disciples receiving Jesus' warning. Jesus remains outside the frame. The dough and starter are an imaginative reminder of His comparison of the Pharisees' hypocrisy to leaven; the verse does not describe a baking demonstration or condemn bread. The scene conveys crowding without depicting trampling injuries.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three bearded men in ochre, blue and russet mantles stand beneath an olive tree. One bows his head with clasped hands; another speaks toward the right with one hand on his chest and the other extended. Warm light falls across a stone terrace, a clay jar, distant pale buildings and hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The sorrowful speakers imaginatively represent the people bringing Jesus the report of Galileans whose blood Pilate mingled with their sacrifices. Jesus remains outside the frame; the killing is not depicted. The terrace, olive tree, clothing colors and number of messengers are artistic choices, not details specified by this verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Six robed men sit around a low wooden table with bread, clay cups and a jug, looking intently toward the foreground. Warm light fills the stone room, with cushions, a recessed shelf and a window overlooking distant houses.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The imagined household meal centers on bread and the watchful guests, reflecting the verse's Sabbath hospitality and close observation. Jesus remains outside the picture, in the direction of their attention. The room, clothing and individual faces are artistic reconstruction; the verse does not specify them. Human artwork review remains pending.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of a crowd in long robes gathered in a sunlit stone courtyard beneath an olive tree. Seated and standing men and women look attentively beyond the right edge. A man in a burgundy mantle holds a small leather pouch at his waist; pink flowers climb the wall.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The listeners gathering and looking toward Jesus outside the frame imagine the verse's movement of tax collectors and sinners drawing near to hear Him. The courtyard, clothing and pouch are illustrative details, not details supplied by the verse. The pouch suggests a tax collector; appearance does not establish who is a sinner. Jesus is not depicted, and human artwork review remains pending.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor courtyard scene: a richly dressed seated man listens to a standing messenger who gestures toward a concerned manager holding rolled scrolls. Terracotta jars, grain sacks and baskets fill the limestone storeroom, with olive trees beyond the arch.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined estate scene illustrates the report brought to the rich man about his manager. The jars and grain represent possessions entrusted to his care; the messenger and courtyard are illustrative details. No act of theft or waste is shown, preserving the verse's distinction between accusation and demonstrated wrongdoing. Jesus, who tells the parable to his disciples, is outside the image.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of an empty sunlit ochre road winding between low plastered houses, shaded wooden doorways, stone steps and terracotta jars. Date palms and flowering vines rise above the walls, with dry hills beneath a blue sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The onward road through an imagined Jericho setting illustrates entering and passing through. Jesus remains outside the picture. The houses, palms and household details are artistic setting choices; the empty street does not mean the verse says Jericho was deserted. No later event is depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An older bearded man in cream robes and a terracotta mantle kneels with closed eyes and open hands in a sunlit stone courtyard. A clay lamp burns on a low bench beneath olive branches; distant rooftops and hills appear through an arch.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined courtyard prayer illustrates the teaching introduced in the verse, rather than an event it narrates. The man's worn face and steadfast posture suggest praying without losing heart. The lamp and dawn suggest persistence through time; they do not promise an immediate answer. Jesus is outside the image, and God is not depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three bearded men in long earth-colored robes sit beneath an olive tree, looking intently toward the right. Angular stones and a thorn branch obstruct the foreground path. A low stone wall leads toward sunlit hills and a distant village.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The obstructed path imaginatively pictures occasions of sin; the verse does not report a literal stone incident. The sober listeners evoke the disciples receiving Jesus' warning, while Jesus remains outside the frame. Their concern recalls the woe He pronounces on the person through whom stumbling comes.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of flatbreads in a linen-lined basket on a wooden table beside a bowl of flour and rolling pin. Pottery, flowers and olive branches surround a stone courtyard overlooking robed travelers on a path toward a sunlit walled city.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The flatbread preparation and travelers nearing the city imaginatively evoke the approaching Feast of Unleavened Bread, called Passover. The courtyard, objects and travelers are illustrative details, not events specified in the verse. The scene conveys anticipation rather than a feast already underway.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of robed men and women seated in a sunlit stone temple courtyard, listening toward someone outside the frame. A solemn group of older religious leaders approaches beside tall columns; one carries a rolled scroll.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative temple composition places the listeners in the foreground and the approaching chief priests, scribes, and elders behind them. Jesus remains outside the frame; the listeners' attention evokes His teaching and proclamation of good news. Architecture, clothing, faces, and the carried scroll are illustrative details, not details specified by this verse. Human artwork review remains pending.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three men in richly patterned robes stand beside wooden offering chests in a sunlit stone temple courtyard. The central man drops coins into a flared bronze opening while holding a leather purse; another reaches into his pouch, and the third waits. Colonnades and steps recede behind them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The donors and falling coins picture the rich people putting their gifts into the treasury. The viewpoint suggests an observer looking up while Jesus remains outside the image. The architecture, clothing, number of donors and shapes of the offering chests are imaginative historical details, not specifications in this verse. Their expressions do not claim motives, and the widow from the following verse is not included.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three women in long robes and head shawls walk along a rocky garden path at dawn. One carries a basket with stoppered jars and folded cloth; another holds a lidded vessel. Olive branches frame the pink-gold sky, with pale limestone, small flowers, distant hills and buildings beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The women and carried vessels illustrate the arrival with prepared spices. Their number, clothing, containers and garden details are imaginative, not details specified in this verse. The rocky destination suggests the burial place, with its entrance out of view; no later discovery is depicted. Dawn light conveys the early hour. Jesus is not shown. Human artwork review remains pending.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A watercolor crowd of men in long earth-colored robes walks across a sunlit stone courtyard toward a columned portico. A lone Roman official in a pale robe and red mantle stands in its shaded doorway. Limestone walls, distant rooftops and cypress trees frame the scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The moving assembly and waiting official illustrate the group leading Jesus to Pilate. Jesus is concealed within the crowd rather than directly portrayed. The courtyard, portico, clothing and dawn light are imaginative historical setting details, not details specified by this verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Men and women in long earth-toned robes gather in a sunlit stone room, seated on woven mats and low benches. Smiling faces turn toward one another beneath timber beams; baskets and clay jars furnish the room, and a window opens onto pale buildings and trees.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The shared room and close gathering picture the verse's emphasis on all being together when Pentecost arrived. The architecture, number of people, clothing and conversational gestures are imaginative staging; this verse does not specify them. The image does not add the miraculous events described afterward.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two men in cream tunics, one wearing a brown mantle and the other a blue-green mantle, ascend broad sunlit stone steps toward a columned temple gateway. Other robed figures walk ahead, and an olive tree shades the left edge.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The two companions ascending toward the temple visualize Peter and John going up for prayer. Warm afternoon light suggests the ninth hour. Their appearance, clothing, other worshippers and architectural details are imaginative setting choices, not details supplied by the verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a bearded man in a terracotta mantle receiving silver coins from another man over a low stone wall. A woman in blue with an ivory head covering stands beside him. Cultivated beds, olive trees, distant stone houses and hills fill the sunlit landscape.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The couple and exchange of coins visualize Ananias and Sapphira selling property. The buyer, cultivated parcel, clothing and transaction gestures are imaginative period details, not specified in the verse. This image illustrates the sale alone, without depicting the later deception or judgment.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of two robed men addressing a seated crowd in a sunlit stone courtyard. Five serious men approach beneath a colonnade: two in pale robes, a central man in a blue mantle, and two elders in darker robes. Leafy branches shade the listeners.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The approaching group represents the priests, temple captain and Sadducees coming upon the speakers while they address the people. Clothing, faces, courtyard architecture and the arrangement of listeners are imaginative historical details. The scene stops at their arrival and does not add an arrest or violence. Human artwork review remains pending.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor travelers leave a walled city along branching paths through olive-covered hills. A woman holds a child’s hand beside a bearded man carrying a bundle. A younger woman supports an elderly woman, while several men remain near the gate.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined departure pictures the believers scattered from Jerusalem under persecution. Their bundles and sorrowful faces suggest forced displacement; their mutual care conveys restrained hope. The men remaining near the gate allude to the apostles staying. Saul’s consent to the killing is part of the verse but is outside this selected view. The particular travelers and landscape arrangement are artistic details, not identified historical portraits.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone chamber, a seated gray-bearded man in cream robes and a blue mantle extends an open hand toward a standing man seen from behind. Three robed elders listen from stone benches beneath warm golden light.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The seated questioner represents the high priest asking whether these things are so. His open hand and the attentive listener picture the exchange. The chamber, clothing, elders and listener are imaginative staging; this verse itself supplies only the high priest and his question. No accusations or later events are depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three elderly women in head coverings sit with empty clay bowls in a sunlit stone courtyard. A concerned man gestures toward them while another listens thoughtfully. Behind them, people gather and volunteers distribute bread and food at a wooden table.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The imagined courtyard places the overlooked widows and their empty bowls beside a busy daily food distribution. The concerned conversation represents the Hellenists' complaint against the Hebrews. Clothing and faces do not mark a racial divide; the distinction is linguistic. The setting, individuals and gestures are artistic reconstruction, and the scene leaves the neglect unresolved as this verse does.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a stern bearded man in a russet mantle leaning forward and gesturing toward an older priest in layered ivory robes at a shaded stone doorway. Sunlit steps, olive branches, clay vessels and a small burning lamp surround them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The imagined courtyard stages Saul approaching the high priest. His tense face, clenched mantle and insistent gesture convey the threats and murderous intent named in the verse without depicting an attack. The architecture, clothing and lamp are artistic reconstruction; the threatened disciples remain outside the picture.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A man in an ochre cloak speaks with open hands to attentive robed men and women in a sunlit stone courtyard. An olive tree shades the listeners; a clay jug stands nearby, and an arched gateway frames a winding road, village and hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The listening gathering imagines the apostles and fellow believers in Judea hearing that Gentiles also received God's word. The messenger, courtyard and particular listeners are illustrative choices, not details specified by the verse. The scene depicts news being heard rather than the Gentiles receiving the word in this same place.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A gray-bearded Roman centurion in mail armor and a red cloak holds a crested helmet and twisted staff in a sunlit stone courtyard. Two soldiers stand beneath an arch behind him. Flowers, pottery and a blue harbor with sailing boats complete the watercolor scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative introductory portrait connects Cornelius with the military rank and Caesarea setting named in the verse. His appearance, courtyard, harbor view and accompanying soldiers are artistic setting details, not events or descriptions supplied by Acts 10:1. His upward gaze does not depict a vision; no angel or later episode is shown.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two robed men stand among a large gathering in a sunlit stone hall. One speaks with an outstretched hand while his companion stands beside him. Seated listeners lean forward with attentive faces and gentle smiles beneath timber beams; an open doorway reveals distant buildings and hills.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined synagogue gathering illustrates the messengers speaking in Iconium and many Jewish and Greek hearers believing. The architecture, clothing, faces and gestures are artistic choices, not details supplied by the verse. The listeners’ receptive expressions suggest faith; their ethnicity and inward belief cannot be established from appearance.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Five men in cream tunics and blue, rust, green and ochre mantles sit around a low wooden table with a blank unfurled scroll, clay jug and lit oil lamp. One gestures as the others listen. Flowering vines frame a sunlit stone courtyard and an arch overlooking tiled rooftops.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined house-church gathering represents the five prophets and teachers named in Antioch. Their faces, clothing, positions and courtyard are artistic choices, not recorded portraits or a specific meeting described in the verse. The shared scroll suggests teaching; Herod is not shown because the verse mentions him only to describe Manaen's upbringing.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone courtyard, a crowned ruler in crimson gestures from a portico. One armored guard grips an older robed man by the upper arm while another blocks the path. A younger man stands beside the older man, and a veiled woman clasps her hands in concern.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The courtyard, guards and unnamed believers imaginatively convey Herod putting forth his power to mistreat some of the church. The grip and blocked path show coercion without graphic injury. The verse does not specify this arrangement or these individuals; the church is represented by people rather than a building. No later arrest, execution or rescue is asserted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two cloaked travelers with shoulder bags and walking staffs approach an open stone meeting house. Wooden benches and a rolled scroll are visible inside. Sunlit terracotta roofs, blue water and distant hills fill the background of the watercolor.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The travelers arriving beside a synagogue picture the destination named in the verse. Their number, appearance, the coastal view and the building with benches and a scroll are imaginative setting details, not a documented reconstruction. The winding road suggests the preceding journey through Amphipolis and Apollonia; those cities are not separately shown. The image does not add the preaching described later.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of an older traveler in a terracotta mantle greeting a young man in blue-green robes. A woman with a cream head covering watches from a stone doorway beside a clay jar. Olive branches, flowering plants, village roofs and distant hills surround the sunlit courtyard.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The imagined courtyard greeting connects the arrival in Derbe and Lystra with the introduction of Timothy as a disciple. The woman represents his believing Jewish mother; her presence and the gestures are artistic choices, not details stated in the verse. His Greek father is not pictured, and the scene makes no claim about the father's faith. The verse's glosses are supplied from the Berean Interlinear, not GBT approval. Human artwork review remains pending.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of seven robed men in a sunlit stone courtyard beneath leafy vines. A standing teacher holds a rolled scroll and raises an open hand, while a companion stands beside him and five seated listeners watch thoughtfully. Travel bundles, woven mats and clay jars surround the group.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The courtyard and individual faces are imaginative. The two standing travelers and listening brothers visualize the teaching encounter reported in Acts 15:1. The rolled parchment suggests their appeal to Mosaic custom without invented writing. Circumcision is not pictured; the teachers' claim that it was necessary for salvation is explained in the verse note, not endorsed by the composition.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded traveler in a cream tunic and rust-colored cloak walks along a stone road toward sunlit buildings and columns beneath a rocky hill. An olive tree, golden grasses and colorful flowers frame the watercolor scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The traveler approaching the city imagines the arrival in Corinth after departure from Athens. His clothing, satchel, road, plants and city buildings supply an illustrative setting; the verse does not specify these details or the route. No meeting or teaching scene is added.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a traveler in a rust mantle greeting three robed men on a stone lane beneath an olive tree, with pale ancient buildings, columns, a winding road and distant hills behind them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The traveler represents Paul finding disciples in Ephesus after his inland journey. The road and hills suggest the upper regions. Their appearances, greeting gestures, architecture and the three visible disciples are imaginative choices; this verse gives no exact group size. Apollos remains outside the scene because he was in Corinth.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of a balding, bearded traveler in an ochre mantle and leather satchel addressing gathered men and women. He rests one hand on a man's shoulder and opens the other toward his listeners. Stone arches, leafy branches, and a sunlit road frame the group.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The traveler represents Paul encouraging the disciples and taking leave after the uproar has ceased. His satchel and the road suggest his departure toward Macedonia. The courtyard, clothing, individual appearances, and precise gestures are imaginative staging; the verse does not specify them. The peaceful gathering depicts the aftermath, not the uproar itself.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a bearded man in a rust-colored mantle standing on stone steps, one hand at his chest and the other extended toward younger men and gray-bearded elders. The listeners sit and stand beneath a stone arch beside a flowering vine in warm sunlight.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The open hand and attentive, serious listeners visualize the respectful request to hear a defense. Younger men and elders evoke the address to brothers and fathers. The courtyard, steps, clothing, faces and arrangement are imaginative details, not specified by this verse; the picture does not establish the listeners’ agreement. Human artwork review remains pending.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Five robed men travel in a wooden sailing boat beneath a glowing cream sail. Coiled ropes, a woven basket and clay jars rest aboard. Two distant figures wave from a stone harbor, while turquoise water and pale coastal hills surround the vessel.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The departing boat and small farewell figures imaginatively connect the company drawing away from their companions with their direct sea passage. The vessel, travelers and harbor are illustrative details, not a documented reconstruction. The distant coast evokes the onward journey; Cos, Rhodes and Patara are successive stops, not three places shown together. Human artwork review remains pending.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of Paul in a cream tunic and rust mantle standing in a sunlit stone chamber, one hand against his chest and the other extended toward robed council members seated on curved stone benches. An arched opening reveals distant buildings and trees.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Paul's steady gaze and respectful open hand picture his address to the council; the hand on his chest suggests his testimony about a good conscience before God. The chamber, clothing and individual faces are imaginative historical staging. The illustration does not portray God or claim to establish Paul's sinlessness. Human artwork review remains pending.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of a robed advocate holding a rolled document and addressing a seated Roman governor. An older white-bearded man and two elders stand behind the speaker; Paul stands apart in an ochre mantle. Two guards flank the dais amid sunlit stone columns, with a harbor visible beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative reconstruction places Ananias and the elders behind Tertullus as he presents their case against Paul to the governor. Paul stands apart as the accused. The clothing, chamber, guards and harbor are illustrative setting details, not details stated in this verse; the image does not specify the charges or depict a verdict.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded man in cream and ochre robes stands with one hand extended toward a seated ruler in a plum robe and gold circlet. The ruler opens a hand toward him while listeners sit behind them in a sunlit stone hall with columns and arches.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Paul's extended hand and Agrippa's open gesture visualize the verse's movement from permission to spoken defense. The audience hall, listeners, clothing and appearances are imaginative period details, not descriptions supplied by this verse. The scene does not illustrate the later content of Paul's defense.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three men in tunics, cloaks and sandals walk along a rising stone road toward a sunlit walled city and its elevated temple precinct. The leading gray-haired man wears a russet cloak with purple trim. Olive trees, limestone rocks, golden grasses and small wildflowers fill the watercolor landscape beneath a blue sky.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The uphill road and Jerusalem destination illustrate the movement stated in the verse. Festus is imagined as the leading Roman official; his appearance, clothing, two companions and the detailed landscape are illustrative choices, not details supplied by the text. The image does not depict the three-day interval or claim that the journey lasted three days.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of three chained prisoners beside a moored wooden sailing ship. A bearded man in a cream robe and ochre cloak stands between two companions, facing a helmeted Roman officer in a red cloak while another soldier gestures toward them. Clay jars and coiled ropes rest on the sunlit stone quay.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The harbor handover imagines Paul and the other prisoners being placed in Julius’s custody for the planned voyage to Italy. The ship, clothing, faces, chains and quay details are artistic reconstruction, not details specified by the verse; the calm scene does not depict arrival in Italy or the later shipwreck.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: In a golden stone courtyard, a bearded man in a rust-colored cloak points at another man holding out stained palms. The accusing man has the same brown stains on his own hands. Olive branches, flowers, a clay pot and a shaded doorway surround the two men.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative courtyard tableau illustrates Paul's teaching rather than a recorded event. The matching hand stains represent shared wrongdoing: the accuser bears what he condemns in the other. The verse does not specify stains, these men or this setting; dirt itself is not presented as sin.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Five travelers in long tunics and ochre, blue, rust and muted green cloaks stand or rest on a rocky coast. An older bearded man holds a staff and a hand to his chest. Blue-green water, pale limestone hills, small flowers and driftwood fill the shore beneath clouds opening to warm light.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The travelers safely on firm ground picture the verse’s deliverance, while the island coast evokes Malta. Their faces, clothing, gestures, landscape and clearing light are imaginative details, not a record of the exact landing place or how they learned the island’s name. The picture adds no later fire or snake episode. Human artwork review remains pending.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An elderly gray-bearded man in ivory robes and a rust-colored mantle sits beside a woven tent with one palm open. A wooden staff rests nearby, while olive trees, wildflowers and sunlit hills fill the landscape.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative portrait recalls Abraham, the forefather named in the verse. His thoughtful expression and open hand invite reflection on Paul's question about what Abraham discovered. The tent and hills provide an imagined patriarchal setting; the verse does not describe this scene or supply its answer here.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two bearded men in long robes sit across a wooden table beneath an olive tree. One raises an open palm while the other rests his chin on his hand. A tied parchment scroll lies between them, with sunlit stone walls, hills and a village beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined conversation gives visual form to the verse's questions, rather than depicting a recorded event. The questioning hand and thoughtful listener suggest reflection; the closed scroll evokes Jewish religious inheritance. Circumcision, the covenant sign expressly named in the verse, is not shown. The picture leaves the questions open.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A woman with open hands and a man with one hand over his heart sit beneath an olive tree. Both wear long robes. A winding stone path passes wildflowers and olive trees toward an empty wooden cross on a distant hill in golden dawn light.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative devotional setting illustrates an abstract teaching, not a narrated event. The resting believers and open hands suggest faith and grateful peace with God. The distant empty cross points indirectly to Jesus Christ, through whom that peace comes; the verse does not describe this garden or explicitly mention a cross. No divine figure is portrayed. Human artwork review remains pending.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A thoughtful man in a cream tunic and terracotta mantle stands beside a muddy patch and a loop of muddy footprints in a sunlit stone courtyard. Clear water pours into a fountain beside a folded cloth, olive branches and flowering plants.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined courtyard is not an event reported in the verse. The returning muddy footprints picture continuing in sin, while the freely flowing fountain suggests abundant grace. The traveler pauses over the question; the mud neither supplies nor increases the water. The comparison illustrates the mistaken inference Paul raises, without portraying sin as a way to obtain grace.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three men of different ages sit around a broad blank parchment scroll on a wooden table. The middle man gestures toward it while the younger and elderly men listen. Warm light filters through an olive tree in a stone courtyard, with hills visible through an arch.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined study gathering represents the address to people who know the law. The scroll stands for the law, and the listeners of different ages suggest its authority throughout a person's living years. The verse does not narrate this meeting; the scene is an illustration of its teaching.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three smiling adults in long robes gather beneath a flower-covered stone arch in a sunlit courtyard. A seated man holds his hands open, while a woman and a standing man rest hands on their chests. Open iron shackles lie on the paving. An olive-lined path leads toward an empty cross on a distant hill.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative courtyard scene illustrates the assurance of no condemnation for those in Christ Jesus. The open shackles suggest release from a condemning judgment, and the believers' peaceful gratitude reflects that assurance. The distant empty cross points to Christ without portraying him. The verse does not narrate this gathering or mention shackles, an arch, or a path; these are visual metaphors, not a historical reconstruction.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A graying, bearded man in a cream tunic and rust-colored mantle sits at a wooden table, one hand on his chest and the other holding a reed pen above blank parchment. An ink pot rests nearby. Through a stone arch, families gather in a sunlit village among flowering plants.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative writing scene presents Paul as the personal example in his argument: his hand at his chest recalls his statement that he too is an Israelite. The families suggest the people to whom he belongs. The courtyard and village are illustrative choices, not a location or gathering described in this verse; no appearance of God is implied.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded man in a cream tunic and rust-colored mantle sits at a wooden table, one hand over his heart and the other palm open. A blank scroll, reed pen and ink bowl lie before him. Olive trees and stone rooftops appear through an archway in warm daylight.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined portrait of Paul uses a hand over his heart and an open palm to suggest sincere testimony and conscience. The writing table evokes his epistle; the verse does not describe this room or these gestures. Christ and the Holy Spirit are not depicted, and the sunlight is ordinary daylight.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded man in a cream tunic and rust-colored mantle kneels on a woven mat, bowing his head with one hand over his heart and the other open. Beyond a low stone wall, adults and children gather among sunlit stone houses, olive trees, pottery and a donkey.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined scene represents Paul's heartfelt intercession: his hand over his heart suggests his desire, and his open hand suggests prayer to God for others' salvation. The courtyard community gives a visible focus for his concern. The verse does not specify this setting or report the people's response, and the picture does not claim that they have already been saved.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: In a warm terracotta courtyard, a man in an ochre tunic opens his hands toward an empty place on a wooden bench. A cloaked newcomer stands by the doorway, while a seated woman gestures kindly toward the seat. An olive tree shades pottery and a low table with cups and a jug.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined household welcome illustrates receiving someone weak in faith without making their reasonings a subject of contention. The open seat and gentle gestures express fellowship; the newcomer’s hesitation suggests uncertainty, not physical weakness. The verse does not describe this particular meeting.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three robed adults pray in a sunlit stone courtyard. A man stands with open palms, a woman kneels with open hands, and another man holds a hand over his heart. Grapevines, clay pots, a basket and garden tools surround them; olive trees and distant houses lie beyond the wall.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined courtyard gathering pictures the whole-body dedication Paul urges, rather than an event narrated in the verse. The believers remain alive and unharmed, offering themselves in willing worship through prayerful bodily postures. Their ordinary surroundings suggest daily life devoted to God in response to His mercies; no figure represents God.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone courtyard, a man with lowered head and open hands stands before a seated magistrate holding a rolled scroll. Three townspeople stand behind the man, and an attendant waits beside the magistrate. An olive tree, pottery, columns and tiled roofs frame the watercolor scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined Roman-era civic encounter illustrates subjection to governing authority through a respectful posture before a magistrate. It is not a recorded event from the verse. Paul grounds existing authority in God's appointment; God is not depicted, and the image does not claim that every action of an official is divinely approved.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a woman in terracotta robes and a cream head covering offering a clay cup to an older seated woman. Two other adults sit beside a low table with bread and a pitcher, beneath flowering vines overlooking a blue harbor and wooden boat.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: Phoebe offering a cup imaginatively illustrates her service to the church at Cenchrea and the fellowship conveyed by calling her our sister. The verse commends her but does not describe this activity, her appearance, or this courtyard; the harbor evokes the named coastal setting.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone courtyard, a younger man bends to support a basket of bread, grapes and a clay vessel held by an older man stepping down from a threshold. A woman reaches toward the older man beside flowering vines, an empty chair and an olive tree.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined act of sharing a laden basket makes patient support visible. The companions accommodate the older man instead of pursuing their own ease, illustrating the duty to bear with others. The verse teaches responsibility toward the weak; it does not narrate this courtyard event or equate weakness in faith with age or physical frailty.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of a bearded man in a brown mantle seated on a low stool, speaking with an open hand to five attentive adults in a sunlit stone courtyard. A clay lamp and jug rest on a low table beneath olive branches.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined courtyard gathering pictures Paul's plain, brotherly proclamation through a humble seated speaker and attentive listeners. The setting, clothing and household objects are artistic details, not details supplied by the verse. God is not depicted; the scene illustrates the manner of proclaiming His testimony rather than claiming to picture the testimony itself.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two bearded men in long linen tunics and earth-colored mantles handle tied scrolls in a sunlit stone courtyard. One kneels beside an open wooden chest and offers a scroll to the man seated at a table with more scrolls and a burning oil lamp. Vines, an olive tree, pottery and distant hills surround them.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative household scene illustrates stewardship rather than a recorded event. The servants carefully tend an entrusted collection of scrolls, suggesting the responsibility of Paul and his fellow workers as servants of Christ and stewards of God's mysteries. The scrolls are an analogy for the entrusted message, not a literal depiction of the mysteries. Neither Christ nor God is pictured.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of an older bearded teacher extending an open hand toward four adults in a sunlit stone courtyard beneath grape leaves. One man bows his head, two listeners turn toward each other, and a seated man looks toward the teacher. Clay pottery and distant buildings complete the scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined courtyard gathering visualizes Paul addressing adult believers with patient concern. Their uneven attention suggests the spiritual immaturity he calls being fleshly and infants in Christ; the verse does not mean literal babies. The setting and gestures are illustrative choices, not details supplied by the verse. Christ is not depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Four robed adults gather around a low table in a sunlit stone courtyard. A cloaked man gestures as he speaks; one listener bows his head into his hand, a woman clasps her hands, and another man listens with his hand at his chin. A tied scroll and lit clay lamp rest on the table beneath flowering branches.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative gathering illustrates the report being heard, not a meeting described by the verse. The listeners' sober faces suggest the gravity of Paul's news. The man and his father's wife are not depicted; their sexual relationship remains offstage. The courtyard, messenger, scroll and lamp are artistic setting details, not facts supplied by the verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A bearded man in a cream tunic and rust-colored mantle sits at a wooden table, looking at a blank scroll. An oil lamp and ink pot stand beside it. Olive branches shade the sunlit stone courtyard; pink flowers, tiled rooftops and blue hills appear beyond an arch.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The imagined solitary reader and blank letter evoke the Corinthians' written concerns; his quiet composure suggests abstinence. The verse does not describe this courtyard or identify this man. The scene does not imply that ordinary compassionate contact with women is forbidden.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone courtyard, a bearded man in terracotta and blue encourages a younger man as they set a stone onto a low wall. A smiling woman holds a basket of stones. At left, a seated man lifts his chin while holding a blank scroll; a dish of cooked meat rests behind him.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined courtyard is a visual meditation, not a recorded event. The self-important scroll holder represents knowledge that puffs up; shared construction and personal encouragement picture love building others up. The untouched meat recalls the question of food sacrificed to idols without deciding whether anyone should eat it. No divine figure is depicted.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Two robed men disagree in a sunlit stone courtyard. One holds a rolled document and gestures toward a seated magistrate beside a guard. Three people sit beneath an olive tree to the right, where an older man extends an open hand. Columns, flowers and a distant harbor fill the watercolor setting.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined Corinthian courtyard places the disputants between a civic tribunal and fellow believers. The rolled document suggests litigation; the seated community makes visible the saints whom Paul says should hear their dispute. The scene illustrates his rebuke, not a recorded lawsuit, verdict or completed reconciliation. The supplied English token glosses are attributed to the Berean Interlinear, not GBT approval.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A watercolor of a balding, bearded man in a cream tunic and russet mantle addressing five smiling adults in a sunlit stone courtyard. One hand touches his chest and the other opens toward them. Leafy vines, pottery, tiled roofs and a distant hilltop building surround the gathering.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined gathering pictures the Corinthians as the living fruit of Paul's labor in the Lord. His hand toward his chest and open gesture toward the people connect his defense of his apostleship with their lives. The verse does not narrate this courtyard meeting. Jesus remains out of view; the picture does not depict Paul's having seen Him or turn ordinary sunlight into a divine figure.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Three travelers in long robes walk along a sunlit path through olive trees. A balding, bearded man in a red mantle leads a man and a woman. Footprints continue ahead around the bend toward distant houses and hills; wildflowers grow beside the path.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined journey pictures imitation through a shared path: the followers walk behind Paul, while footprints already ahead suggest the example of Christ that Paul follows. Jesus is outside the picture. The verse gives a command to imitate, not an account of this journey; the landscape and footprints are visual metaphors.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor families in earth-colored robes walk along a dry, stony passage between towering turquoise waters. A father holds a child's hand, elders carry bundles, and a long procession stretches toward distant hills beneath a broad luminous cloud.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative reconstruction pictures the ancestors' shared passage through the sea beneath the cloud recalled by Paul. The families, clothing, gestures, light and arrangement are artistic details, not particulars stated in this verse. The many travelers emphasize its repeated "all"; no human figure represents God.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Six modestly robed adults gather in a sunlit plaster courtyard. A seated man holds a blank-facing papyrus scroll and gestures as five companions listen. Olive branches frame the scene; a clay lamp, jug and bowl rest in the foreground. Warm watercolor textures enrich the clothing and walls.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined gathering pictures believers receiving instruction through Paul's letter. Their shared attention relates to his desire that they understand spiritual matters. The verse does not describe this courtyard or gathering, nor specify a manifestation of gifts; the scene supplies a setting for attentive learning rather than inventing a miracle.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Warm watercolor of a courtyard gathering: a seated bearded man gestures as adults listen, while a younger woman offers an earthenware cup to an older woman. Vines shade ochre walls, with pottery, woven mats and a garden beyond an arch.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined gathering connects the command to pursue love with the desire for spiritual gifts, especially prophecy. The unnamed speaker represents a believer addressing the assembly, while the offered cup illustrates loving care. The verse does not narrate this courtyard event, and the image does not identify the speaker as Jesus or claim to show an actual prophetic message. Human artwork review remains pending.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: Watercolor of a sunlit stone courtyard with a large bronze disc suspended in a wooden frame and two bronze cymbals on a ledge. Behind them, a man in ivory and terracotta gestures while an elderly man in a blue mantle sits with bowed head and clasped hands beneath an olive tree.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined courtyard places the verse's bronze and cymbal comparison beside speech that leaves a nearby listener overlooked. The separated gazes suggest missing loving attention. It is a visual meditation, not a recorded incident or a portrait of Paul; human and angelic tongues are not depicted literally, and the instruments do not imply that music itself is wrong.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An older bearded teacher in an ochre mantle gestures toward five attentive adults in blue, olive and rust robes. They stand on sunlit stone paving beside a limestone doorway, flowering vines and olive branches, with a coastal town beyond.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imaginative courtyard gathering connects the teacher and attentive listeners with the gospel proclaimed and received. Their feet on firm paving echo standing in that gospel. The verse does not specify this meeting, setting or these appearances; the scene is a visual meditation rather than a documented event.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: In a sunlit stone courtyard, a woman lowers a coin into an earthenware bowl on a wooden table. Another woman watches warmly while an older bearded man holds open a linen pouch. Loose coins, clay jars, and olive branches complete the watercolor scene.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: This imagined gathering illustrates the collection for the saints and the shared obedience Paul asks of the Corinthians and the churches of Galatia. The coins and pouch make the collection visible; the courtyard and these particular donors are artistic choices, not details narrated by the verse.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: An older bearded man in a cream robe and russet mantle sits with his chin resting on his hand in a sunlit stone courtyard. A leather satchel and wooden staff lie beside him. Olive branches, flowering plants and a clay jug frame an empty road leading toward a distant harbor.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The seated figure imaginatively represents Paul considering his decision. His set-down satchel and staff suggest a journey paused, while his sober expression recalls sorrow. The courtyard, empty road and harbor are illustrative settings, not details stated in the verse; no visit is shown.

scenes_chirho.alt_chirho: A torn and patched cloth tent sags on a rocky hillside dotted with small flowers. Above it, an ivory house with a glowing open doorway rests among blue, lavender and golden clouds.
scenes_chirho.reading_note_chirho: The failing tent visualizes Paul's image of our mortal bodily life. The intact, light-filled dwelling among clouds imaginatively contrasts it with the eternal home from God, not made by human hands. The house is a visual metaphor, not a claim about heaven's architecture or a depiction of God. No historical event is being illustrated.
